title: FTSE Russell — December 2026 Periodic Review Announcement: preliminary additions, deletions and indicative shares/float published after the close (four weeks before implementation)
source: EST: owner-published date, stated FIVE independent times across four documents and reproduced from the stated rule. (1) FTSE Russell's reconstitution page, lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/russell-reconstitution, re-fetched 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200), verbatim: "Beginning on November 13, the preliminary lists are communicated to the marketplace, and updates are provided on November 20, November 27, and December 4". (2) FTSE Russell, "FAQ Document Russell US Equity 2026" (lseg.com dam policy-documents PDF, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 content streams inflated and text-extracted in-session 2026-09-06), whose dated December 2026 calendar column gives "Indicative Review Products circulated (including REIR) | 13 November 2026". (3) THE SAME FAQ STATES THE RULE, and it is new to this chain: "Periodic Review Announcement: Additions, deletions, and indicative shares in issue and free float data are published in advance of the June and December review implementations. For the June review, this information is published on the fifth Friday prior to the effective date, and for the December review, on the fourth Friday prior to the effective date." Counting Fridays back from the 2026-12-11 implementation gives 12-04, 11-27, 11-20, 11-13 -- the fourth is 2026-11-13; the same count on June 2026 (implementation 06-26) gives 05-22 as the fifth, which is the date FTSE Russell's own 2026 schedule press release publishes. (4) FTSE Russell, "Insights from the November 2025 Russell US Indexes parallel run", Index Insights, February 2026 (lseg.com dam research PDF, HTTP 200, 585,342 bytes, 28 content streams inflated in-session) -- a document no sibling lane has read -- whose Exhibit 1 schedule column "Dates to be used for effective date of 2nd Friday in December" gives "Indicative Review Products circulated (including REIR) | 13-Nov-26". (5) Ground rules v7.2 (August 2026) Appendix F gives the December leg "Preliminary Information Released = Four weeks prior to implementation", and 2026-11-13 to 2026-12-11 is exactly 28 days. Filed estimate because this calendar's confirmed-tier prefixes have no member for an index owner's own published schedule -- the same prefix gap the russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 ledger banked; promote when one is added. Canonical file written by the russell-recon-preliminary-2026-11-13 initial research 2026-09-06, superseding proposals/russell-recon-preliminary-2026-11-13.from-russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11.json (read in full first)
notes: THIS IS THE INFORMATION EVENT; russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 is the execution event. TWO THINGS PUBLISH ON THIS DATE AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS PUBLIC -- the single most operationally important fact here, and it is what makes the December leg scoreable at all. The FAQ's "Indicative Review Products circulated (including REIR)" are the Russell Monitor List Suite (RML, RML Extended, REIR), which the same FAQ states is "available to subscribing clients only". The PUBLIC artifact is the Periodic Review Announcement -- "Additions, deletions, and indicative shares in issue and free float data" -- and FTSE Russell's own 2026 schedule press release gives its mechanism verbatim: "Preliminary index additions & deletions membership lists posted to the website after 6 PM US eastern time". So the counts are observable without a subscription, and BECAUSE THEY POST AFTER THE CLOSE the first tradeable session is Monday 2026-11-16, not 2026-11-13. SIZE, FROM THE OWNER'S OWN SIMULATION rather than a model: the February 2026 parallel-run paper's Exhibit 7 publishes measured December-leg numbers the sibling lanes did not have. Russell 2000 -- June 2025 actual 235 adds / 173 deletes / 10.43% turnover; November 2025 simulated December leg 141 adds / 119 deletes / 5.37%. The simulation's drift window was five months (June 2025 rank day 2025-04-30 to the parallel rank date 2025-09-30) against December 2026's six (2026-04-30 to 2026-10-30), so scaling gives roughly 154-169 on the owner's greater-of-adds-or-deletes convention and 285-312 on a naive adds-plus-deletes count -- and FTSE Russell states it "will apply buffers in the December reconstitution implementation to help reduce turnover" where the parallel run applied none, which pushes the realised figure toward the low end. THE SCOPE ASYMMETRY IS NOW QUANTIFIED, not merely directional: December simulated turnover as a fraction of June 2025 actual runs 0.37x for the Russell 1000 and 0.51x for the Russell 2000 core, but only 0.06x / 0.12x for the R1000 growth/value pair and 0.28x / 0.22x for the R2000 pair -- the style leg is where December is cut, exactly as Appendix F's rules say. THE PROPOSER'S "no macro confound at all" IS CORRECTED: 17 tracked events sit within five days of 2026-11-13, including ppi-2026-11-13 (medium) on the day itself, cpi-2026-11-10 and us-china-tariff-truce-expiry-2026-11-10 (both high) three days before, and retail-sales-2026-11-17 (high) two sessions after. The corridor is clean for the COUNT (a published document is immune to macro) and dirty for the TAPE. All four preliminary-update dates collide too: 11-20 is opex-2026-11-20, 11-27 is thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27, 12-04 is jobs-2026-12-04, 12-11 is the implementation plus a funding deadline and a CR expiry. Impact low, and the tier is a call rather than an inheritance: this session measured a real June-cycle effect on the session after publication (IWM minus SPY excess return, mean +0.71%, 6 of 7 positive, n=7), which argues for medium -- but the effect fully round-trips by T+4, December's leg carries a third to a half of June's turnover, no house playbook is index-flow-keyed, and symbols is deliberately EMPTY so the deterministic screen cannot trip on small-cap beta. Promote to medium if 2026-11-16 replicates the June effect. Kind sector matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane.
